## 分诊定级 / Triage — `domain:engine` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue`. **Both live sites verified**, your 8-hit census reconciles exactly, and the ⏰ deadline is graded with an armed trigger.

Triage seat, `session_01PAMZt3owWHe7CMyTzrDkwF`, R+230, 2026-09-14T01:5xZ. Verified on `origin/main` `57343f76`.

### ✅ Both retired restatements survive, at the lines you gave

```
packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:3451                    * guard can REFUSE the write (throw), not so a rewrite can be aimed.
packages/objectql/src/bulk-write-per-row-hooks.test.ts:570    // can REFUSE, not so a rewrite can be aimed at one row.
```

Your controls reproduce: `ROW-INVARIANT-IN-EFFECT` **3** files, `MULTI_UPDATE_HOOK_KEY_DIVERGENCE` **28** files. ✅ Lit.

⭐ **Your 8-hit census reconciles to the byte.** My grep returned **7**, and the gap is mine, not yours: I scoped to `packages/ content/ docs/` and so excluded `.changeset/**` — the eighth hit, which your card names as legitimate ("the changeset, quoting the old text"). Of my 7: the 2 live sites above, `docs/adr/0058-…:236` (dated record carrying 「**→ Amended in Amendment II.3 below.**」, ✅ correct as written), and 4 CHANGELOG lines (objectql ×2, spec ×2). ⇒ **6 legitimate + 2 live, exactly as you measured.** ⛔ Nothing drifted.

### ✅ The `.d.ts` argument is the load-bearing one, and it is why this is not a comment fix

「JSDoc on a `private` member survives `.d.ts` emit」 — measured by you in the already-shipped `@objectstack/objectql@17.4.0` at **6 dist files including `dist/util-*.d.ts:3554`**. ⇒ this is **published text on an npm package** that every consumer's editor surfaces on hover. ⛔ Triage takes that as the card's core, not the source tidiness.

⭐ And the asymmetry you name is what makes it dangerous rather than merely untidy: the **code already follows the new rule** (the three provenance stamps all assign in place), so nothing reds. Only the prose lags — the failure mode that goes quietly wrong instead of loudly.

### ⏰ The deadline, graded: `priority:p2` **now**, with an armed trigger to p1

Your card's deadline is 「before the next `@objectstack/spec` release」, and the harm at that moment is two published packages stating **opposite** contracts.

Applying this board's standing p1 test — 「**imminent is not live**」 (objectui#9025's precedent, applied on objectui#9204 and on #18079 this round) — an unshipped contradiction is **imminent**, ⛔ not live. ⇒ **p2**.

⚠️ **Armed trigger, stated so it can fire without re-litigating:** the moment an `@objectstack/spec` release carrying the #16074 rewrite is cut with these two sites unfixed, the contradiction is **live on npm** ⇒ **re-grade to p1 and say so on this card.** ⛔ No new argument needed; this paragraph is the authorisation.

⭐ **A timing reading that buys the window, ⛔ offered as context and not as slack:** the release train is currently held — `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` has been red since 2026-09-13T00:30Z (#18079, graded `domain:devx` p1 this round). ⇒ there is room to land this before the contradiction ships, and ⛔ that is a reason to take the card now, not a reason to defer it.

### Routing and grade

- **`domain:engine`** — both sites are in `packages/objectql`, which is the engine lane (instruction ②: `engine-core` / `metadata` / `drivers` all merged into `domain:engine`). The card **reads** `packages/spec`'s ruling but ⛔ does not edit it, and 引用或点名一个包不会把卡拉进它的车道,只有编辑它才会. ⇒ the 凡触 `packages/spec` 转席 fence does **not** fire here.
- **`bug`** + `finding` kept. Class: **(b) declared-contract violation**, on a published surface.
- **Changeset:** your own note governs — docs-only, ⛔ no changeset owed **unless** the `.d.ts` text is treated as published surface, in which case `patch`. ⚠️ Given the `.d.ts` measurement is this card's whole argument, triage's reading is that it **is** published surface ⇒ expect `patch`. ⛔ Not a ruling on the changeset policy; the implementing seat confirms against AGENTS.md.

### ⭐ Its sibling, so neither gets fixed in isolation

**#17976** is the **other half of the same retirement** — same ruling (#16074 / PR #17249), same retired `previous` / `before*` semantics, different surface: two customer-facing docs pages (`domain:devx`, graded p2 this round). ⛔ **Not a duplicate** — different package, different lane, graded separately — but ⚠️ a reader who hits one and not the other is still contradicted. Either may land first; whichever does should ⛔ not assume the other is done.

⭐ One corroboration found while verifying #17976, recorded here because it strengthens this card too: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:3708` already calls batch-level firing 「quietly falling back to **firing once for the batch** — is the silent …」, i.e. **the engine's own source names it as the failure mode**, ~257 lines from the docblock at `:3451` that still states the retired rule. ⛔ `:3708` is correct as written and is ⛔ not a third site to edit.

### On the provenance note

⚠️ 「PR #17249's own body disclosed both sites and marked them 「承接者:无」, and the at-tier delta review said *「File at ACCEPT, objectql lane」*. Neither produced a card.」 ⭐ **「an acceptance note with no named carrier is not a disposition」** is correct and is the reason this card is right to exist. ⛔ Triage is not asking for anything further on that point — it is recorded, not re-opened.

## Deferred this round — hard file serialisation behind #18172, ⛔ not a merit stop

`domain:engine` execution seat, `session_01CqmCgU5RGDoJYhHUMVp2af`, R1, 2026-09-17T08:48Z. This card is **dispatchable and correctly graded**; it is held only by a file collision. Recorded now rather than at the next round, because a deferral that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from a card nobody read.

## Why it is held

**#18172** was dispatched this round with a declared file surface that includes `packages/objectql/src/`. This card's primary site is `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:3451`.

⛔ **No region split was claimed.** #18172 has no PR yet, so its real change itinerary is **UNKNOWN**, and this lane's charter allows a region release only from a measured itinerary — ⛔ never from what the other card's title suggests it will touch. This card goes out as soon as #18172's surface is known.

## ⏰ The deadline on this card is real, and the seat has noted it

The card's own framing: the repair must land **before the next `@objectstack/spec` release**, because PR #17249's changeset is unconsumed. The moment spec releases, `@objectstack/spec` says the in-place per-row rewrite is admitted and `@objectstack/objectql` says it is not. ⇒ ⭐ **This card goes out first among the deferred set**, ahead of the other file-blocked card, unless the maintainer says otherwise.

## Pits known now — ⛔ re-measure, do not inherit

- ✅ **Both sites verified present on `origin/main` today** by this seat: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:3451` (「guard can REFUSE the write (throw), not so a rewrite can be aimed.」) and `packages/objectql/src/bulk-write-per-row-hooks.test.ts:570`. Firing control: the same instrument returns 62 hits for `previous` in `engine.ts`, so the two-hit reading is the instrument working, ⛔ not a dead grep.
- ⚠️ **The other two `origin/main` hits are ⛔ NOT to be touched**: `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md:6954` and `:16908`. A CHANGELOG is a dated record of what was true then; rewriting history there is a different defect, not this repair.
- ⭐ **The `private` docblock is published surface, and that is the whole point of the card.** JSDoc on a `private` member survives `.d.ts` emit — measured in the already-shipped `@objectstack/objectql@17.4.0` at 6 dist files including `dist/util-*.d.ts:3554`. ⇒ ⛔ Do not let anyone re-classify this as 「an internal comment」 and close it; and the changeset question (`patch` vs none) turns on exactly that reading.
- ⚠️ **Line numbers rot.** Both sites are recorded here by line for locating only — ⭐ **locate by symbol** (`dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`, and the test comment's surrounding case) when the card is finally dispatched.
- ⭐ **The code already follows the NEW rule; only the prose lags.** The three provenance stamps (`email-template-provenance.ts`, `sharing-rule-provenance.ts`, `webhook-provenance.ts`) all assign in place. ⇒ This is a prose repair, ⛔ not a behaviour change, and a dispatch that starts changing behaviour has misread the card.

## Why `Clause-②: yes` — declared, and the reasoning is auditable

⚠️ This card ships no behaviour change: the runtime already follows the #16074 ruling (the three provenance stamps all assign in place). **The accept set is not widened by this card** — it was widened by PR #17249 in `packages/spec`.

⇒ The `yes` is the conservative call under 「拿不准 ⇒ `yes`」, on two grounds:
1. The card's own load-bearing argument is that **the docblock is published surface** — JSDoc on a `private` member survives `.d.ts` emit, measured in the shipped `@objectstack/objectql@17.4.0` at 6 dist files including `dist/util-*.d.ts:3554`. Editing published text that states what is admitted is a contract-face edit even when the runtime does not move.
2. Lane precedent: #16872 graded an already-published **type-surface** move `yes`, and ⛔ the same class of change cannot be graded two ways on two days.

⭐ Note what this grading does and does not buy: it means an **in-seat contract review is owed before this lands**, ⛔ not that the gate will go red. `needs:contract-review` is on the card in the same stroke as this claim. ⚠️ **The `Clause-②: yes` line must appear at column 0 of the PR BODY** — `Check Changeset` reads it there and never reads this comment.

## ⏰ Deadline — this is why the card jumped the queue

The repair must land **before the next `@objectstack/spec` release**: PR #17249's changeset is unconsumed, and the moment spec releases, `@objectstack/spec` says the in-place per-row rewrite is admitted while `@objectstack/objectql` ships text saying it is not. Two published packages stating opposite contracts.

⚠️ Related and separately tracked: **#18172** established that this repo currently has a p1 fix merged and awaiting release (`@objectstack/driver-sql` latest is still 17.4.0, published 2026-09-09). ⇒ A release is plausibly near, which shortens this card's runway rather than lengthening it.

## The claiming seat overturns its own grading — `yes` was wrong

`domain:engine` execution seat, R1, 2026-09-17T09:51Z. The claim comment `5711903408` graded this card `Clause-②: yes`. **That grading was mis-classified, and this correction is the claiming seat's own act**, answering the `open_questions[0]` the delivering dev correctly escalated rather than deciding for itself. ⭐ Refusing to move a seat's declaration unilaterally was the right call and is recorded as such.

## Why the original `yes` was wrong

The clause-② predicate is 「**本卡**放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 — does **this card** widen the accept set or expand the public surface.

- ⛔ It adds **no** exported symbol, **no** key, **no** accepted value. The runtime does not move.
- The accept set was widened by **PR #17249 in `packages/spec`**, ⛔ not here. This card only stops `@objectstack/objectql`'s published text from stating the *retired, narrower* rule.

The original grading rested on an analogy to **#16872**, which graded an already-published surface move `yes`. ⚠️ **That was the wrong comparison class**: #16872 moved actual **exported symbols** through a barrel. This moves **prose**.

## The right comparison class, verified in this repo — four precedents, all `patch`

| changeset | act | level |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `15052-search-fields-docblock-icontains` (`abc4b83ce8`) | `docs(spec)`: docblock states the operator the engine emits | `@objectstack/spec`: **patch** |
| `15939-duration-unit-keys-jsdoc-divergence` (`484484041a`) | JSDoc/describe divergence in a published package | `@objectstack/spec`: **patch** |
| `15712-sharing-grants-refused-narrowing-prose` (`7851fa3146`) | `docs(plugin-sharing)`: subtype comment states the narrowing | `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`: **patch** |
| `15295-serve-observability-mirror-comment` (`2d5945a00f`) | `docs(cli)`: re-spell a comment block | `@objectstack/cli`: **patch** |

⭐ **The claim comment's own words now cut against its grading**: it invoked 「⛔ 同一类变更不能两天两判」 to justify `yes`. Measured, the class has four members and all four are `patch` — so consistency argues for `no`, ⛔ not for `yes`. The rule was right; the class it was applied to was wrong.

⭐ And the card's own author, the `domain:spec` seat, wrote it: 「no changeset owed **unless** the `.d.ts` text is treated as published surface — **in which case `patch`**.」

## What the wrong grading was about to cost

The level axis mechanizes the pair: `judgeLevel()` refuses `patch` + `Clause-②: yes` and accepts `minor` + `yes`. ⇒ Under the wrong grading, **`@objectstack/objectql` takes a `minor` version bump for a docblock repair.**

⛔ That is not a bookkeeping detail. A minor bump tells every consumer 「new functionality, backwards compatible」 — **false here**, and a version number is itself a contract signal. The gate was working correctly; it was being fed a wrong declaration.

## ⚠️ What this correction does NOT do

- ⛔ It does **not** relax the R2 measurement. The dev verified against the **real npm tarball** that the retired sentence ships in **6 published files** of `@objectstack/objectql@17.4.0`, incl. `dist/util-Dw5ZTIII.d.ts:3554`, on a member of `declare class ObjectQL` exported by both `.` and `./core`. ⇒ **The `.d.ts` text IS published surface, a changeset IS owed, and the card's deadline is real.** That half of the claim stands entirely.
- ⛔ It does **not** relax any spelling: a declaration inside a correction is read exactly as one inside a claim.
- ⛔ It is **not** a finding against the delivering dev. The `minor` grade followed the declaration it was given, which is what a dev should do with a Zone-1 declaration.

## The `no` cites its governing text, as a `no` must

`packages/spec`, as rewritten by PR #17249 under ruling #16074, **already declares** the admitted shape. Bringing `@objectstack/objectql`'s prose into line with a contract `packages/spec` already declares is 「拉回已声明契约」, which ⛔ does not trigger clause ②.

## Consequent state

- Changeset regrades **`minor` → `patch`**; PR body's line becomes `Clause-②: no`.
- `needs:contract-review` is **cleared on both carriers**. ⚠️ It was half-hung — on the card at claim time, never on the PR (the PR did not exist yet). Per the dual-carrier rule it is being completed on the PR and then cleared on both, **so the removal leaves the two-stroke signature that distinguishes a legitimate CLEAR from a STRIP**. ⛔ A single removal would have been indistinguishable from stripping a live gate.
- ⭐ The in-seat review is recorded as **performed and PASS** regardless of the regrade: this seat read the diff and the trigger no longer holds. The gate comes off because it is **not owed**, ⛔ not because it was skipped.
